clue.text: A chap casting line in the bay

indicators.note: casting here means throwing something into the mix, paired with in to say a piece is put inside
in, after casting, says the line goes inside the phrase a chap

parts.note: cove is old British slang for a chap or fellow

explanation.surface: A man stands casting a fishing line out into the waters of a bay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'casting ... in' says L (line) is thrown into A COVE, landing between the A and the COVE.
explanation.definitionFit: An alcove is a recess in a wall, a bay in the architectural sense.

clue.text: Strict copper poked inside an old banger

parts.note: taken as the letter A

indicators.note: poked inside says the copper symbol is thrust into the old car

parts.note: a crate is slang for a rickety old car; banger is British slang for an old car
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A stern policeman is jammed into a rusty old car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' suggests a police officer but is CU, the chemical symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: Accurate means precise and exact, the sense in which a strict account is correct.

clue.text: Pointedly ignore young woman producing weapon

parts.note: to cut someone is to snub them deliberately
lass is a word for a girl or young woman

explanation.surface: Someone snubs a girl who brandishes a weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutlass is a short curved sword, once used by sailors.

clue.text: Provide justification for opening of variety show

indicators.note: opening of means just the first letter of variety is taken

parts.note: to indicate is to show or point out

explanation.surface: Someone defends their choice of opening act for a variety show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'show' looks like a theatre noun but is the verb INDICATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To vindicate is to clear or justify, show to be right.

clue.text: Moved camp

explanation.surface: Someone shifted the tents to a new campsite.
explanation.definitionFit: Moved in the emotional sense is touched or stirred; camp means mannered and showy, i.e. put on for effect.

clue.text: Be short of brass, but sense effect of wind

explanation.surface: Someone is hard up, and also feels a chilly breeze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brass' is British slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to suffer financial hardship; literally it is to sense a cold current of air.

clue.text: Newspaper article in French up-set composer

indicators.note: up-set in a down clue means the pieces are set upwards, read in reverse

parts.note: a rag is a disparaging word for a newspaper
le is a French definite article

explanation.surface: A newspaper article in French upset a composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up-set' reverses RAGLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward Elgar was an English composer.

clue.text: Old hero from America inferior to the ones here?

indicators.note: inferior to means lower down, so in this down clue America's letters sit below the other piece

parts.note: these means the ones here, close by
US is short for the United States of America

explanation.surface: An ancient hero from America is lesser than today's folk?
explanation.walkthrough: 'inferior to' places US below THESE in the down grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Theseus is the Greek mythological hero who slew the Minotaur.

clue.text: Give some aid on a team

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone offers a bit of help to a team.
explanation.definitionFit: To donate is to give, especially to a cause.

clue.text: It's played, following quiet agreement with club, right away

parts.note: piano is the musical direction for quiet
an accord is an agreement

indicators.note: away says the right letter is sent off from the golf club

parts.note: an iron is a golf club

explanation.surface: A game resumes after a quiet deal with the club, with the right man gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'away' removes R from IRON, leaving ION.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a musical instrument with keys and bellows, something played.

clue.text: Counts for nothing, as tea, say, does in 22

explanation.surface: Something is worthless, like iced tea in some puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: 22 is NOTICE: tea, abbreviated T, cuts the letters NO ICE in two to make it, so the phrase describes exactly what T does there.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for having no influence or making no impression is this phrase about ice.

clue.text: Ingenuous description of Llewellyn's valley

explanation.surface: An innocent portrait of a Welsh valley in a novel.
explanation.walkthrough: Richard Llewellyn wrote the novel How Green Was My Valley, set in a Welsh mining valley.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingenuous means naive and inexperienced, as a green newcomer is; the novel's title describes the valley with this colour word.

clue.text: Dress again in regal ensemble

indicators.note: an ensemble is a group put together, so the letters of regal and in are assembled afresh

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone changes into a grand royal outfit once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ensemble' reads as an outfit, but it signals rearranging REGALIN; 'Dress' is the military sense of lining up troops.
explanation.definitionFit: To dress ranks is to line soldiers up straight, so dressing again is putting them back into line.

clue.text: Peak charge for water that's coming down fast

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill or peak, as on Dartmoor in England
rent is the charge paid for a property

explanation.surface: A mountain site levies a fee for water supply.
explanation.definitionFit: A rushing, fast-flowing stream of water is called a torrent.

clue.text: Her name could be turned to advantage

indicators.note: turned means flipped round, so the word for advantage is read from its end to its start

parts.note: an asset is an advantage or benefit

explanation.surface: A woman's name might be used to her benefit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be turned' reverses ASSET.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a woman's first name, so it is a name a woman might bear.

clue.text: A contemptible person, he's going back inside pub

indicators.note: inside says one piece sits within the word for a contemptible person

parts.note: a louse is a mean, contemptible person

indicators.note: going back means the letters of he are read in reverse

parts.note: the 's is just the verb is; the word he gives its letters

explanation.surface: A despicable man is heading back into the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'he's' is just 'is' and gives no letters; 'going back' and 'inside' are the two indicators, with A standing at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: An alehouse is an old word for a tavern or pub selling beer.

clue.text: Excessively exhausted, lashed out unreasonably

explanation.surface: Someone worn out also spent wildly.
explanation.definitionFit: Spent means tired out, so too spent is worn out to excess; lashed out also means spent money freely.

clue.text: Sort of cutie not typical of the Germans

indicators.note: sort as a verb means arrange, so the letters of cutie not are put in another order

explanation.surface: A kind of sweetie unlike most Germans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sort of' signals the anagram of CUTIENOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Teutonic relates to the Teutons, the ancient Germanic peoples, and so means German in character.

clue.text: One can suppress reports of missiles being launched

definitions.text: One can suppress reports of missiles being launched

parts.words: One can suppress reports of missiles being launched
parts.note: reads as an anti-missile censor, but reports are the bangs of gunshots and the device muffles them as bullets leave a gun

explanation.surface: Someone can hush up news of a rocket launch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reports' suggests news, but a report is also a loud bang; 'missiles' are bullets.
explanation.definitionFit: A gun attachment that muffles the noise of firing is this device.

clue.text: State of Jones when shot

parts.note: reads as a wounded man's condition, but it is an American state that is also the first name of a film hero called Jones, shot in the cinema sense

explanation.surface: How a man named Jones was after being hit by a bullet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' suggests a gunshot wound, but it means filmed: the adventurer in the films.
explanation.definitionFit: A US state shares its name with the whip-cracking film archaeologist Jones.

clue.text: Person with organisational duties initially spelt out

definitions.text: Person with organisational duties initially spelt out

parts.words: Person with organisational duties initially spelt out
parts.note: the initials of a master of ceremonies, M and C, written out in full as their letter names

explanation.surface: An organiser's role is first explained clearly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' points at the initials MC, and 'spelt out' turns those letters into their spoken names.
explanation.definitionFit: A master of ceremonies, who runs an event, is known by the initials MC, and this is how those sound.

clue.text: Attractive woman receiving injury in church run

indicators.note: receiving means the church abbreviation takes another piece within it

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
harm is damage or injury
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A lovely woman gets hurt on a church fun run.
explanation.walkthrough: The page splits 'in-jury' across a line break; read it as the single word injury. 'receiving' is the container signal, and 'in' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A charmer is a delightful, attractive person who wins people over.

clue.text: Attention given to unsatisfactory employees

explanation.surface: Bad staff are being warned to pay attention.
explanation.definitionFit: Notice means attention or heed; it is also the warning of dismissal handed to staff.

clue.text: Senior citizen's daughter in case, abandoned by husband

indicators.note: abandoned by means the husband's letter leaves the result
in says the daughter's letter is placed within the word for a case

parts.note: a holster is a case for a gun

explanation.surface: An elderly woman's daughter is involved in a divorce case after her husband walked out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts D inside HOLSTER, and 'abandoned by' removes H, leaving the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An old person, a senior citizen, is informally called this.

clue.text: Anyone who's broke can't stand it

definitions.text: Anyone who's broke can't stand it

parts.words: Anyone who's broke can't stand it
parts.note: seems to say the penniless hate something, but to stand someone a drink or meal is to pay for it, which the broke cannot afford

explanation.surface: People without money cannot bear something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stand' means pay for, as in standing a round of drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: Paying for someone's drink or meal is this kind of indulgence offered to another.

clue.text: Parvenu gets off after appearing for trial

indicators.note: after places the word for gets off behind the word for appearing in court

parts.note: to be up before a court is to appear for trial
to start is to get off the mark, set off

explanation.surface: A social climber is acquitted after appearing in court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets off' suggests acquittal, but it means START, set going.
explanation.definitionFit: A parvenu is someone newly risen to wealth or status, a social climber.

clue.text: How umpire, referee or judge concludes it's senseless

parts.note: the riddle asks how each official's title ends, and the reply begins 'in an', naming the letter that closes the word

indicators.note: concludes points at the final letter of the official's title, the letter that word ends with

explanation.surface: Every sports official ending up with a pointless decision.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a riddle: how does umpire, referee or judge conclude? 'In an E', since all three titles end with E; the E is picked from judge, where 'concludes' sits.
explanation.definitionFit: Inane means silly, foolish and lacking sense.

clue.text: Small furry creature, one in much distress

indicators.note: distress means the letters of one in much are put under strain and knocked out of order

explanation.surface: A tiny animal, one of many, is badly upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in much distress' reads as the creature's state, but 'in' is part of the fodder ONEINMUCH.
explanation.definitionFit: The ichneumon is a mongoose, a small furry carnivore.

clue.text: Tough partner no longer playing

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
acting is playing a part

explanation.surface: A hard-hearted former partner has stopped performing.
explanation.definitionFit: Exacting means demanding and difficult to satisfy.

clue.text: Get somewhat hysterical about arrangement of atoms

indicators.note: somewhat says only part of the following word is used, a stretch of its letters

explanation.surface: Someone gets a bit worked up over atomic structure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somewhat' gives a run inside 'hysterical'.
explanation.definitionFit: In chemistry, steric relates to the spatial arrangement of atoms in a molecule.
